title: 16 GiB host-to-device upload, then 16 GiB download
job: Upload 16 GiB from pinned host memory to GPU 0 as 16 queued 1 GiB copy-engine copies, then download 16 GiB back the same way: NVBandwidth host_to_device_memcpy_ce followed by device_to_host_memcpy_ce with --bufferSize 1024 --loopCount 16.
derivation: h2d bytes = 16 copies × 1 GiB = 17,179,869,184 B; the same for d2h
copy-mode async: NVBandwidth queues all 16 copies of one direction on a stream before they start, so napkin charges the fixed copy latency once per direction
serial: the download starts after the upload finishes, so the two transfer stages add

observation.tool: NVIDIA NVBandwidth v0.10.0 (commit 82fc4e8c), copy-engine memcpy testcases
observation.metric: median CE bandwidth per direction over --testSamples 7, converted to time as bytes / bandwidth; observed time = upload + download

tolerance.why: The bandwidth constants are bulk 512 MiB pinned copies on the same kind of link, and the predicted time is almost all bytes / bandwidth (the fixed latency is 2 × 9.8 μs of about 0.6 s). NVBandwidth and napkin-bench agreed within 2% on H2D and D2H at 512 MiB (PR #25), so ±10% leaves room for host-to-host variation among PCIe Gen5 x16 Modal hosts, but not for a different link generation.

match: PCIe link Gen5 x16 during the copies, the link the profile was measured on; a Gen4 host halves host bandwidth and is a different system, not a miss
pinned host memory and copy-engine copies, as in the calibration
excludes: the host wait: NVBandwidth times copies with CUDA events while a spin kernel holds the stream, so its time excludes the issue and synchronize cost that napkin's one async latency charges (2 × 9.8 μs)
NUMA placement: --disableAffinity is required on Modal, so host buffers are not pinned to the GPU's NUMA node
pageable memory, which would add a staging copy
overlap of upload and download: the job is serial by construction
